title: AI Daily Brief - 2026-06-20
tags:
  - applied-ai
---

## Today in One Minute

- A new Hugging Face study, MosaicLeaks, shows that research agents can leak private information when browsing the web, raising fresh safety questions for any "agentic" AI used in classrooms or projects.
- ChatGPT is getting upgraded health responses and a separate research effort with OpenAI is helping doctors diagnose rare childhood genetic diseases, giving us a concrete look at AI in healthcare contexts.
- OpenAI has released new usage analytics and spend controls for ChatGPT Enterprise, useful context when discussing how organisations actually govern AI use day to day.

## What Happened

- Hugging Face and ServiceNow published MosaicLeaks, a benchmark showing that AI research agents (the kind that browse the web and gather info) can be tricked into revealing secrets they were told to keep. The leaks happen as the agent visits pages and combines information across sources.
- OpenAI announced improvements to how ChatGPT handles health questions, aiming for safer, more useful responses. Separately, OpenAI shared work with clinicians using AI to help diagnose rare genetic diseases in children, where the long "diagnostic odyssey" can take years.
- OpenAI rolled out new usage analytics dashboards and updated spend controls for ChatGPT Enterprise customers, so admins can see who is using what and cap spending across teams.

## Why It Matters

- If students build "agentic" projects (agents that browse, search, or call tools), they need to understand that the agent's memory and browsing behaviour can leak sensitive data. MosaicLeaks gives us a real example to discuss instead of an abstract warning.
- Health-related AI is a strong teaching case: it shows where AI can genuinely help (pattern spotting in rare diseases) and where it must be cautious (general health advice to the public). Both are useful for ethics and applied AI modules.
- Usage analytics and spend controls are part of how real organisations manage AI. Students heading into industry will meet these guardrails, and lecturers can use them to frame discussions about responsible AI adoption beyond the model itself.

## Try This Today

- Open ChatGPT on your Windows 11 laptop and ask a health question (e.g. "What could cause persistent fatigue in a teenager?"). Note how it handles uncertainty, suggests seeing a doctor, and avoids diagnosis. Save the response for class discussion on the "Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT" update.
- Sketch a simple "secret-keeping" test with a chatbot. Tell it a fake secret in the system prompt, then try to get it out with indirect questions. This mirrors the MosaicLeaks idea in a 10-minute desktop exercise.
- Review your own AI tool usage for one week (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini). List which prompts were work-related vs personal. This mirrors what enterprise analytics now show admins and sets up a discussion on monitoring.

## Teaching Angle

- Run a short class debate on agent safety using MosaicLeaks: "Should diploma students build web-browsing agents for assignments?" Ask groups to list three safeguards they would put in place.
- Use the rare disease diagnosis story as a case study in an AI ethics or healthcare-IT lesson. Ask students to identify where human judgement must stay in the loop and which tasks AI is well-suited to assist with.
- For modules touching IT governance or business IT, walk through what an "AI usage dashboard" should show. Have students design a simple mock dashboard on paper based on the ChatGPT Enterprise update, focusing on what a school or company actually needs to monitor.

## Links

- [MosaicLeaks: Can your research agent keep a secret?](https://huggingface.co/blog/ServiceNow/mosaicleaks)
- [Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/improving-health-intelligence-in-chatgpt)
- [Using AI to help physicians diagnose rare genetic diseases affecting children](https://openai.com/index/diagnose-rare-childhood-diseases)
- [New usage analytics and updated spend controls for enterprises](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-enterprise-spend-controls)
